physical_harm: Indiscriminate cuts caused over the body using aruval resulting in death; injuries to sons of victim
premeditation_planning: Court found premeditation/planning as the accused unlawfully assembled with a common object to murder
key_evidence_accepted: The injuries found on the person of the deceased are duly supported by medical evidence as well as corroborated by the deposition of PW-1. The concurrent findings have been recorded by the courts below in this regard. The trial court recorded the finding that the FIR had been lodged promptly. The evidence of a hostile witness cannot be discarded as a whole, and relevant parts thereof which are admissible in law, can be used by the prosecution or the defence.
witness_credibility: PW-2 turned hostile but supported the case of the prosecution with regard to one of the accused, thus, his evidence is reliable. The deposition of PW-3 has no force as he could have improved his version if he were not truthful. The evidence of PW-1 is reliable as she could identify the appellants even in the darkness.
trial_duration: Trial court acquitted all accused; High Court upheld order; Supreme Court dismissed appeal
legal_representation: Shirin Khajuria for the appellants; M. Yogesh Kanna for the respondent
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court acquitted all accused; High Court upheld order; Supreme Court dismissed appeal
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellants were involved in the murder of Ramasamy, as evidenced by the FIR, medical reports, and the deposition of PW-1, who specifically named both appellants. The trial court and High Court found sufficient light for identification, and the injuries were supported by medical evidence. The prosecution also emphasized that the evidence of PW-2, though hostile, was reliable in parts and supported the case against the appellants.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the courts below had acquitted 15 accused persons based on the same evidence, and therefore, the appellants could not have been convicted. They also claimed that the identification of the appellants in darkness was not possible, and the evidence was inconsistent and unreliable.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that even if major portion of the evidence is deficient, the court must separate grain from chaff, and the maxim 'falsus in uno, falsus in omnibus' does not apply in India. The court also emphasized that the evidence of a hostile witness cannot be discarded as a whole, and relevant parts can be used.
precedent_relied_upon: Atluri Brahmanandam (0) Thr. LRs. v. Anne Sai Bapuji AIR 2011 SC 545; Laxmibai (dead) Thr. L.Rs. & Anr. v. Bhagwantbuva (dead) Thr. L.Rs. & Ors. sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the appellants were found guilty of the offence punishable under Section 302 IPC, and the courts below had already convicted them and sentenced them accordingly. The Supreme Court upheld the conviction and sentence as lawful.
